The construction of a DC Series motor is different from the DC Shunt motor.
In the Shunt Motor, the field coil has many turns of fine wire designed to produce a high resistance.
High resistance is needed to prevent a very large field current that could damage the field coil.
In the Series Motor, the field coil has few turns of heavy wire designed to produce a low resistance.
The low resistance is needed to allow most of E to be felt across the armature. This ensures the armature will rotate.
What type of field coil is used in a DC Series Field motor?
TRY AGAIN!
If a high resistance field coil is used in a DC Series Motor, most of E is dropped across the field coil leaving very little voltage across the armature. The rotor would not rotate..

The next motor characteristic we will discuss is speed control.
The DC Shunt Field Motor uses 2 types of speed control, Armature and Shunt field resistance.
The armature speed control varies the applied voltage.
The Shunt Field resistance speed control varies the value of a resistor in series with the Field Coil.
Let's examine why these two methods of speed control work in a Shunt Field DC Motor.

Now let's investigate motor start currents.................
When a motor is first turned on, there is 0 RPM and 0 CEMF.
Since CEMF is 0, the entire applied voltage is felt across the armature coils. Armature current is maximum.
I decreases CEMF - Increasing I decreases
As the motor begins to spin, armature current as well as total current drawn from the power source, will decrease due to CEMF.
In fact, some large motors have two sets of coils and wires that are controlled by a centrifugal switch.
A heavy duty set of coils is used for starting the motor. This rates the motor for higher starting current.
A normal set of coils is used when the motor is running. This rates the motor for lower running current.
